title: Tools: registerTool Mastery
objective: After this lesson you will be able to define tools with registerTool (names, descriptions, Zod input schemas, titles, output schemas), write sibling-disambiguating descriptions, and rely on SDK pre-handler validation with isError discipline.
why: Tools are how models act — and the #1 tool failure is definitional: vague descriptions mis-select, loose schemas admit garbage, missing output schemas force prose parsing. TS SDK v2 concentrates all three into one Zod schema with framework-enforced validation. Version basis: @modelcontextprotocol/server (v2), zod v4, Node 20+ — registerTool replaces v1's tool().

blocks.text: `registerTool(name, config, handler)` with a Zod `inputSchema` object: the SDK derives the advertised JSON Schema (what the model sees), **validates arguments pre-handler** (bad calls never reach your code), and **infers handler arg types**. `.describe()` on fields survives conversion — it becomes the model's only argument documentation. One schema, three jobs; write it like the contract it is.

blocks.caption: v2 shapes: title, sibling-disambiguating description, Zod schema, structured output

blocks.text: Namespaced names (`lookup-order` vs `search-orders`, `calculator_arithmetic` style) plus **when-to-use sentences naming the sibling** ('For browsing many orders use search-orders instead') eliminate the overlap confusion that plagues toolsets. Titles render for humans; descriptions decide for models. Undescribed siblings get coin-flip selection — describe the boundary, not just the function.

Add `outputSchema` and return matching **`structuredContent`** beside human-readable `content`: machines parse the structured half, models/humans read the text half. Handlers returning both serve dual consumers without format wars. Validation failures surface as `isError: true` results the model can react to (clarify, retry fixed, escalate) — never raw throws across the protocol.

blocks.caption: isError keeps failures inside the protocol — readable, routable, loggable

blocks.title: v1 → v2 migration note
blocks.text: Coming from v1 (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk with server.tool()): run the codemod, rename the package to @modelcontextprotocol/server, convert tool() calls to registerTool(name, config, handler), and move schemas to Zod objects. Title precedence is title → annotations.title → name. Migration is mechanical; mixed-version fleets negotiate via server/discover versions.

blocks.title: Validate like the SDK
blocks.note: Run it: expect ok, then bad-format, then missing — pre-handler rejection with named problems, mirroring SDK validation. Handlers run only on valid args; violations become model-readable isError results.

items: One Zod schema: advertised JSON Schema + pre-handler validation + inferred types; .describe() reaches the model
Namespaced names + sibling-disambiguating descriptions steer selection; titles serve humans
outputSchema + structuredContent serve machines and readers; isError keeps failures routable
v2 registerTool replaces v1 tool(); migrate via codemod + package rename

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice validator on all three cases and map outcomes. (b) Write the registerTool definition for search-orders (query string + limit int ≤50 optional) with a description disambiguating from lookup-order, in real v2 SDK shape. (c) State what the SDK does with {query: 42} (number, not string) before your handler runs.
hints: Outcomes: ok / bad-format:orderId / missing:orderId — pre-handler, named, no handler execution.
Mirror the lesson's lookup-order: title, sibling sentence ('For exact-ID fetch use lookup-order instead'), z.object with .describe()s, limit int max 50 optional.
Wrong-typed args reject pre-handler as isError results: handler never runs, model reads the failure and reacts.
exercise.why: Schema-as-triple-duty (advertise/validate/infer) plus sibling descriptions plus pre-handler rejection are the three v2 mechanics — each verified, with migration knowledge making old code readable too.
exercise.code: // v2 tool template: name + title + sibling description + Zod schema + structured output.

quiz.q: lookup_order vs search_orders, undescribed. Predict + fix?
options: Coin-flip selection between overlapping tools — describe when-each with sibling sentences; descriptions are the model's only docs
quiz.explain: .describe() survives into advertised schemas. Sibling disambiguation ('use X instead for Y') is the highest-value description sentence.

options: SDK rejects pre-handler → isError result naming the violation; handler never runs
quiz.explain: Single-schema validation gates handlers: bad args become model-readable failures, never code paths. Quarantine-with-evidence at protocol level.

quiz.q: v1 tool() code in the wild. Migrate how?
options: Codemod + package rename to @modelcontextprotocol/server + registerTool(name, config, handler) with Zod object schemas
quiz.explain: Mechanical migration: codemod converts calls, packages rename, schemas become Zod objects. Mixed fleets negotiate versions via discovery.

summary: One schema (advertise/validate/infer), sibling-aware descriptions, structured outputs, isError discipline, v2 migration fluency. Definitions steer models.
